title: Ferrotoroidic ground state in a heterometallic {CrIIIDyIII6} complex displaying slow magnetic relaxation

material_class.structural_family: heptanuclear {CrDy6} double triangle (two vertex-sharing trigonal pyramids/tetrahedra)

synthesis.procedure: Aerobic synthesis: Cr(NO3)3·9H2O (0.4 g, 1 mmol) and Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.22 g, 0.5 mmol) were dissolved in MeCN (20 ml), then ortho-toluic acid (0.14 g, 1.0 mmol) and triethylamine (0.55 ml, 4.0 mmol) were added, giving a pale purple solution. After stirring 4 h, the solvent was removed to a purple oil, which was redissolved in MeOH/iPrOH (1:1) and allowed to evaporate slowly. Pale purple crystals of 1 formed within 10–15 days (ca. 25% crystalline yield).
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aerobic solution reaction followed by slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: solvent removed to a purple oil; redissolved in MeOH/iPrOH (1:1); slow evaporation gave pale purple crystals

properties.summary: Heptanuclear {CrIIIDyIII6} cluster with a ferrotoroidic ground state from intramolecular dipolar coupling of two con-rotating {Dy3} triangles. Room-temperature χMT = 87.16 cm3 K mol−1; χMT falls to 14.37 cm3 K mol−1 at 1.8 K (H = 1 T), consistent with Dy Stark depopulation and antiferromagnetic exchange. Low-T M(H) is S-shaped at 2–3 K. AC susceptibility shows a nonzero χ″ down to 1.8 K without maxima (0 and 2000 Oe dc). Micro-SQUID single-crystal hysteresis below 0.8 K (Hc ≈ 0.6 T at 0.03 K, 0.28 T s−1 along a Dy–Dy vector; step at Hs ≈ 0.7 T) indicates SMM-like slow zero-field relaxation enhanced by ferrotoroidic coupling.
